Episode 247. Liberation War of Laprarosa (8)
“Ka-haaat!”
The Tetallon grazed Jin's chest.
Understanding the opponent's strength wasn't just a challenge for Jin. Shimat, too, with his already shattered body, had managed to reach Jin several times.
Bones exposed and organs spilling out, Tetalon only grew sharper. The sword seemed to be transcending even the Battle God’s senses at times.
It appeared to be awakening, like Ron Hiran during the Sword Emperor War, or Jin against Paelito.
It felt as if a relentless evil spirit had latched on. Tetalon, stained red with madness, malice, persistence, and combativeness, was ceaselessly sweeping away the blue thunder.
To Limagas and the other members of the Red Plutonian, it might seem like a futile struggle. But to Jin, Ban, and their companions, it wasn't.
He was still a dangerous enemy and was becoming more dangerous.
Of course, that didn't mean Jin would lose. Victory was already assured. The only matter of concern was when the battle would end and the complete liberation of Laprarosa.
“Hee, what's happening? Hurry and launch it, Immortal. While the Sky Fortress is still Frozen.”
At Yona's words, Veil nodded. He was overwhelmed by the battle between Jin and Shimat.
A battle between Battle God, it was truly indescribable. Even though Jin seemed much stronger, he couldn't easily end Shimat.
'It feels like... watching Temar from the past.'
Veil didn't think of Jin when he thought of Temar.
He was reminded of Temar while watching Shimat – his demeanor in the face of despair, swinging his sword with radiant eyes, the miracles that unfolded every time.
The chains of thunder binding the aerial fortresses were being repeatedly released and refilled.

However, it seemed unlikely that their main cannons would hit Rafararosa again. Even if they briefly recovered from their frozen state, Jin's sword would already have shattered the immobilized cannons like a picture.
Paaaaaa…!

Every time the cannons, consumed by the lightning, were destroyed, a loud noise erupted. The destroyed cannon, engulfed by the red energy of the Red Plutonian, shattered everywhere, dropping fragments resembling massive sapphires.

The fragments, melted by the heat emitted by Jin, converged back into the pulse of the Plutonian Domination Sword. Meanwhile, the four aerial fortresses had significantly reduced in size compared to the beginning.
This was due to over half of their external armor being destroyed. Many of their crew members had perished, and now the fortresses were solely focused on protecting their main cannons.
Even if the red energy cannons couldn't reach, without them, there would be no means of counterattack left.
‘The Tushin brethren's fighting spirit alone can't turn the situation around. We can't inflict enough damage on them for recovery to be impossible.’
The surviving Red Plutonian commanders deeply realized this.
Excluding the Sky Fortress, not a single ship from the fleet remained. In essence, more than 80% of the entire forces, except for Kri, were being annihilated right here.
"Immortal, now's the time!"
Yona threw the liberation device to Veil. The moment he caught the box, Veil felt as though he locked eyes with Shimat for a split second.
He flinched, trying to guard the device, but Shimat now had no interest in Laprarosa's liberation.
He couldn't think of destroying just the device or stopping it somehow. All he was focused on was cutting down Jin.
There were no other options. Fighting with such a luxurious mindset would mean being unable to withstand even a single attack.
"Hmph!"
With all his strength, Veil threw the liberation device towards Laprarosa. It was the moment when the Sky Fortress was frozen, and the dimensional rift was at its largest.
'If there's no problem within the dimension, the liberation device should fall soon.'
'Let's see if we catch it. But, Jin Brother.'
'I think I know what you're trying to say.'
The two were thinking the same thing. They believed it would be better if more allies came to the front.
'Yes... He's getting stronger. It will still take quite some time to end him.'
Variable.
Shimat's fighting spirit was causing rifts in the battlefield that continuously brought in variables. And these variables didn't have to manifest only through the Red Plutonian.
Ziffle, Kinzelo, the Sun God Religion, Ganesto.
Any of them could appear on the battlefield. And Jin was judging that Ganesto was the most likely. After all, it was Ganesto who had lured Shimat to use the original chaos.

From the moment Jin confirmed the original chaos, he had considered the possibility of Ganesto's participation. Perhaps, he even suspected that the quick possibility of fusion with the Battle God might have been due to Ganesto's will.
So far, every situation has turned out to be surprisingly favorable. When the trio of demons appeared, and even now, when the original chaos has been unleashed in the desert.
'However, too many personnel might actually be a detriment. It could endanger the main stronghold of the Jin brothers. Maybe adding just two or three with certainty would be best.'
Jin nodded inwardly and checked Veil's position.
"What are you looking at?"
Seizing the moment, Shimat unsheathed the Red Divine Sword. Jin deflected its crimson wave and quickly approached Veil.
[Bring Luna and Runtia. Send back Yona.]
Veil, without even replying, immediately distanced himself from Jin. Had he reacted a split second later, his body would've been cut in half by Tetalon.
It sent shivers down his spine. It was hard to believe, seeing that Jin was deflecting such a sword several times every second.
"Remarkable, Shimat."
Jin, while keeping distance from Veil, said this in defense.

Shimat now looked like a bloodied mass in human form. His skin was melted away by the wave energy of Plutonian Domination Sword, revealing muscles and bones, and his organs were in such a horrific state they barely looked human.
Yet, his red heart shone intensely even amidst the blue storm. His eyes, fixed on Jin, were unwavering.
[It's a waste to use such determination for an illusory entity like the Sun God.]
"Now, all that doesn't matter. I will surpass you, and die."
[Then, it's a vain awakening. Having lived with the sole intention of resurrecting the Sun God, in the end, you're running at full strength towards a death unrelated to that purpose.]

"Yes, I'm only realizing now. Jin Runkandel... As you said, the Sun God was a mere illusion. We believed in a single path since our birth. But this, it was something we could overcome... Right now, I'm not fighting as a follower of the Sun God."
It was merely to uphold the pride of the Red Plutonian, carrying the weight of being their only Battle God.
Shimat's torn lips curled slightly.

"If I had known deviating from the path was this enjoyable, we would never have fought a single day to revive the Sun God. We would have fought solely with our own strength, to seize the name of Plutonian."
[In the end, the outcome of meeting me would've been the same.]
"Yes, but the process and meaning would have been different. Now, I'm fighting this way for the first and last time."
With a swift motion, Sigmund sliced off Shimat's left arm. The arm vanished into thin air even before it hit the ground, swept away by a surge of energy.
However, moments later, Shimat's body began to glow and smolder with a red hue. Red wave energy engulfed his entire form in an instant.
Only the glowing core and the Tetalon remained where he had stood. Shortly thereafter, from that spot, the red wave energy began to mold back into a human shape.
As if to suggest that the body he had honed over a lifetime was merely a shell, the Shimat that now faced Jin looked like a shadow brought to life in a red hue.
"Now I think I can defeat you, Jin Runkandel."
At a glance, it seemed as if he had overcome death, much like Ron.
However, Jin and Ban recognized what was truly happening. Shimat had merely transformed his deteriorating body into a form suitable for combat, allowing him to continue fighting for a limited period.
This wasn't due to the technical prowess of the Red Plutonian but was realized solely through sheer will.
Once the granted time elapsed, Shimat wouldn't survive. Jin and Ban, with their deep insights, recognized this.
"I'm not sure how long I can maintain this state. An hour? Two hours? Maybe shorter, maybe longer. Either way, it doesn't matter. You won't be able to leave here until my time is up."
[Yes, abandoning my brothers to save myself isn't the way of the Plutonian.]
"Ha ha ha, are you suggesting that our downfall was due to our inability to care for one another? You might have a point there! Isn't that right, my Brother?"
The Red Plutonians couldn't respond to Shimat's call. However, they were all listening intently, eager to hear the last words of their Battle God before their impending death.

"From the absence of Kinzelo, living a life bound by the order of the sun, the Blue Plutonian, to the damned Great Seal. My people, we've never been free from fate. But today, on the brink of our destruction, we live only for ourselves. We fight, we get hurt, and we die."
With a creaking sound, the air fortresses began to move as Shimat's energy slowly pushed back the blue light of the Plutonian Domination Sword.
The glowing cores of the Red Plutonian melted into the power source of the air fortresses, burning fiercely, reminiscent of warriors before their final battle.

"We never felt guilty about oppressing the weak, seizing their lands, and enslaving them. Likewise, we aren't afraid of being trampled upon, tormented, killed, or facing our end by those stronger than us. That's who we are."
In response, the air fortresses launched their cannons. Jin drew his sword, slicing through the attacks raining down from Lafrarosa and locked eyes with Shimat.

[You brag so proudly about being inherently filth, ugliness, and brutality... But even that is better than droning on about the sun god's order and fate, Shimat. Today marks the end of that barbarism and arrogance.]
